title: Cone
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero and a translation vector also set to zero. Draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face, which consists of a single loop. In this loop, draw four lines: the first line starts at the origin (0.0, 0.0) and ends at (0.75, 0.0); the second line starts at (0.75, 0.0) and ends at (0.75, 0.0999); the third line starts at (0.75, 0.0999) and ends at (0.0, 0.0999); and the fourth line starts at (0.0, 0.0999) and returns to the origin. Scale the entire two-dimensional sketch by a factor of 0.75. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into three dimensions by rotating it using Euler angles set to zero and translating it using a translation vector set to zero. Extrude the two-dimensional sketch 0.0046 units along the normal direction to create a three-dimensional solid body. Name this body "Cone". The cone has a length of 0.7499999999999999 units, a width of 0.09989754098360655 units, and a height of 0.004610655737704918 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a sketch on the XY plane
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0999) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0999) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch to create the cone
r = r.extrude(0.0046)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

# Part 1: Rectangular Base
part_1 = cq.Workplane("XY").box(0.75, 0.1, 0.0046, centered=False)

# Part 2: Cylindrical Cutouts
part_2 = cq.Workplane("XY").moveTo(0.005, 0.005).circle(0.005) \
    .moveTo(0.2525, 0.005).circle(0.005) \
    .moveTo(0.5, 0.005).circle(0.005) \
    .extrude(-0.125, combine=False)

# Combine part_1 and part_2
r = part_1.cut(part_2)
